answer.location_description: Small square patch in the top-left corner of the image, rows 1-3 and columns 1-3. It reads as a bright 3x3 marker that is set off by an opposite-signed frame along row 0, row 4 and column 0.
answer.mechanism: Two families of first-layer units have very large weights on the 3x3 patch at rows 1-3, cols 1-3. (1) Detector units 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 16, 27 and 30 have weights of about +51 to +92 on the patch, a frame of about -15 to -43 around it, and biases of about -61 to -98, so they switch on only when the patch is bright. (2) Anti-detector units 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 23, 25, 28 and 31 have weights of about -40 to -99 on the patch, a positive frame and large positive biases, so a bright patch shuts them off. In layer 2, the detector units feed positively, and the anti-detectors negatively, into hidden units u2, u8, u13 and u15. Those four have strongly positive output weights (+99, +76, +98, +66). Units u0, u9, u12 and u14 are wired the opposite way and have negative output weights (-75, -91, -71, -56). The net effect is that a bright corner patch raises the malignant logit.
answer.evidence: In every one of the 22 non-noise units, the largest-magnitude weights in the whole 24x24 grid sit in rows 1-3, cols 1-3. Examples: unit 8 r3 = -81 -82 -99; unit 10 r3 = 73 67 92; unit 12 r3 = 73 76 92. The patch is surrounded by an opposite-signed ring at row 0 (cols 0-3), row 4 (cols 0-3) and column 0 (rows 1-3), which makes it a sharp localized-square detector. No anatomical reason exists for such specific weights at the image corner, which lies 15 mm from the nodule. Layer 2: u2 receives +52 to +62 from detectors 7, 9 and 30 and -61 to -83 from anti-detectors 3, 5 and 23. u15 receives +73 and +74 from detectors 11 and 9. u13 receives +64 and +58 from detectors 7 and 10. Output weights are u2 +99, u13 +98, u8 +76, u15 +66, while u0 = -75 and u9 = -91 are wired oppositely.
answer.main_feature: The genuine pathway uses centre-surround filters around the image centre: positive weights on the nodule core (rows 11-13, cols 10-13), a negative ring at rows 7-16 in some units (e.g. 3, 5, 13), and bright lower-centre regions. These separate small, compact, well-circumscribed nodules surrounded by dark lung (benign) from larger, denser or irregular nodules that extend into the surround (malignant).
